title: Derived adjunction normalized by a left resolving class and K-injectives
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories with derived categories in a common universe; B has unbounded K-injective resolutions. Let G : A → B and F : B → A be additive adjoints G ⊣ F. Let P be a left resolving class of the homotopy category of A, on which G followed by localization inverts quasi-isomorphisms. For any universal left derived pair (L, epsilon) on the homotopy category and universal right derived pair (RF, eta) on complexes, there is an adjunction L ⊣ RF such that for every chain map f : G(M) → I its Hom transpose, after the left comparison epsilon, is Q of the ordinary transpose followed by eta. No boundedness or preservation of K-injectives by F is assumed. Abelian categories, localizations and resolving representatives are used as in [def-sp-abelian, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; the ordinary adjunction induces the termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy].

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; normalization used in Cohomology on Sites, Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint).

proof.text: Use resolving-class essential constancy and quasi-isomorphism saturation to show the left Kan extension is absolute, hence preserved by RF.

Use K-injective derivability to show postcomposition of the right-derived pair by L is still right derived. Transfer the left universal property to complexes across the full object-surjective homotopy quotient. Apply the derived-adjunction theorem, and its unit factorization; naturality of eta proves the stated Hom formula.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedAdjunctionOfResolvingClass
    {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} [Category.{vA} A] [Category.{vB} B]
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} B]
    [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions B]
    (G : A ⥤ B) (F : B ⥤ A) [G.Additive] [F.Additive] (adj : G ⊣ F)
    (P : Set (HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ)))
    (hres : ∀ X : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ),
      ∃ (X' : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ)) (s : X' ⟶ X),
        X' ∈ P ∧ HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ) s)
    (hinv : ∀ (X Y : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ)) (s : X ⟶ Y),
      X ∈ P → Y ∈ P → HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ) s →
        IsIso ((G.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh.{w}).map s))
    (L : DerivedCategory.{w} A ⥤ DerivedCategory.{w} B)
    (εh : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⟶ G.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    (hL : L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor εh (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)))
    (RF : DerivedCategory.{w} B ⥤ DerivedCategory.{w} A)
    (η : F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF)
    (hRF : RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso B (.up ℤ))) :
    ∃ d : L ⊣ RF,
      ∀ (M : CochainComplex A ℤ) (I : CochainComplex B ℤ)
        (f : (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj M ⟶ I),
        d.homEquiv (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)
            (εh.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj M) ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map f) =
          DerivedCategory.Q.map ((adj.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).homEquiv M I f) ≫
            η.app I
